newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm slightly amid slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm slightly amid slack trade.

text.p: Irish bonds were marked up slightly on Monday although dealers described trade as very thin in the absence of market-moving data.

"There's no real news around today but it may also be the case that people are taking a breather after last week's good recovery," one dealer said. "Sentiment looks pretty positive for the week ahead though and there are some interesting figures due."
The market had been buoyed last week by Irish pound strength against sterling, dealers said, while UK PPI figures this morning had been very supportive of gilts.
UK April producer input prices fell 1.9 percent on the month against a forecast fall of 0.5 percent. Output prices were up 0.2 percent against 0.1 percent forecast.

By 1450 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 18 pence from Friday's close at 102.21 to yield 5.82 percent, while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 30 pence from the close at 109.65 to yield 6.46 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 127 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area and at 97 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.

Looking ahead, dealers said, U.S. retail sales figures due tomorrow were arguably the main focus of the week, but inflation data from both sides of the Atlantic -- including U.S. PPI and CPI, and UK average earnings -- expected later in the week would also be watched with interest.
